name: LLM_CHAT
description: A chat-completion model provider. One required action, `chat`: messages in, an assistant message (or a stream handle) out — or, when the vendor answered but the turn failed, a `Failure` the caller can classify without reading error text. The wire shapes here are the harness's own, not any vendor's; a provider plugin translates them to its API. Prose contract in docs/SPI.md. Schemas are documentation and tooling input: Gwead validates no payloads at dispatch.

chat.description: One model turn. With `stream` unset or false the model's whole reply comes back as `message`; with `stream: true` the result instead carries an integer stream handle yielding newline-delimited JSON events shaped by `streamEventShape`.

system.description: System prompt. A top-level field, not a message: `messages` roles are only `user` and `assistant`.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first.

tools.description: Tools the model may call this turn. Derived from TOOL plugins' manifests (each `call` action's `tool` block); absent or empty means no tools.

max_tokens.description: Cap on generated tokens. Optional; the provider applies its own default and ceiling.

stream.description: Ask for the streamed output form.

oneOf.description: The buffered form (`stream` false or absent).

stream.description: A Gwead stream handle: an index into the StreamRegistry the caller attached to this execution, meaningless against any other table (each table numbers its handles from 1; an execution run without a caller-supplied table has its streams drained when it returns). It yields UTF-8 newline-delimited JSON, one `streamEventShape` event per line, ending with an `end` event followed by end-of-stream. End-of-stream without an `end` event means the turn failed mid-stream — an `error` event, when the provider can still say why, is followed by end-of-stream, never by `end`.

oneOf.description: The failed form, buffered path only: the request reached the vendor and the vendor said no — a non-2xx status, or an error document — so the provider can still say why, as data. Failures the provider cannot classify without reading error text (the transport failed, the operator denied the egress, the kernel refused the step) stay step errors, which the caller treats as uniformly fatal to the turn. A streamed turn reports the same failure as its `error` event instead.
An increment of assistant text, to be concatenated in arrival order.

A complete tool call. Providers buffer partial tool-call deltas and emit the call whole: arguments are machine-consumed, so incremental display buys nothing and every consumer would otherwise reassemble JSON fragments.
The final event of every successful stream.

The turn failed and the provider can still say why. Always the last event: followed by end-of-stream, never by `end`. The same three fields as `Failure`, flattened beside `type`. `retryable` marks failures worth repeating unchanged (rate limit, overload) as opposed to ones that will fail again (bad credentials); absent means unknown. `kind` is a provider-specific identifier, informational only.

AssistantMessage.description: May be empty: a refusal, or `max_tokens` hit immediately, can stop a turn before any block completes.

ToolUseBlock.description: The model asks for a tool. `id` is the provider's identifier for this call, echoed back by the matching ToolResultBlock; `input` is arguments per the tool's declared schema.

ToolResultBlock.description: A TOOL `call` result, carried back to the model in the next user message.

Tool.description: A tool offered to the model — a Gwead tool descriptor on the wire. `input_schema` is the JSON Schema for the call's arguments, taken verbatim from the TOOL plugin's `tool.parameters`.

StopReason.description: Why generation stopped: the model finished, the model wants tool results, `max_tokens` was hit, or the model declined to continue (a `refusal` turn must not be retried or continued). A consumer receiving a value outside this enum must treat the turn as failed; adding a value is therefore a contract change, never a quiet extension.

Failure.description: Why a turn failed, from a provider that can still say. `retryable` marks failures worth repeating unchanged (rate limit, overload, a transient server error) as opposed to ones that will fail again (bad credentials, a malformed request); absent means unknown. `kind` is the provider's own identifier for the failure class (an Anthropic `error.type`, say), informational only: consumers branch on `retryable`, never on `kind` or `message`.

Usage.description: Token accounting. Deliberately open: a provider may report extra counters (cache reads, for instance) under its own keys, and consumers must tolerate and may ignore them — only the two required fields are contractual.
